adds.name: Vega State Park (Island)
adds.waterfront_evidence: Esri World Imagery 2024-07-05 (Vivid WV03, 0.31 m, pool near full), frames at 39.2287,-107.7964 with the two occupied site bays plotted: the bays sit on the west edge of the Island peninsula's gravel lot, 65-80 m from the high-water edge (77-91 m to OSM's Vega Reservoir polygon, way 40064055) across grass with scattered oak/serviceberry clumps and a brushy shore fringe, no road or development between; water on three sides of the low peninsula is in view but past the ~50 m bound (lakeview, not lakefront). Dam 1.5 km W; the peninsula is on the pool side, DEM 2431 m at the sites and on the open water, so not below pool.
adds.inclusion_evidence: cpwshop.com (parkID 50045, loop 'Island Campground', loopID 51550) sells sites 403 and 404 as 'Basic' with 'Looking For Category: RV Site,Tent Site,Trailer Site', gravel driveways, 'Maximum Vehicle Length: 60', tent pad, fire pit and picnic table (402 is tent-only, 25 ft); CPW's park page places 'the Island campground and day-use area' on the north side of the reservoir, 'accessed from County Road 64.6', and the CPW brochure map (2024) shows Island Campground on the peninsula, reached by the park road; imagery 2024-07-05 shows the road onto the peninsula on dry ground at near-full pool and RVs parked in the site bays -> real drive-in campground a 23-ft motorhome fits (2 sites). Read 2026-10-27.
adds.note: Vega State Park's smallest campground: two RV sites and a tent site on the Island, a low peninsula on the reservoir's north shore beside the Island day-use area and boat ramp, reached by a gravel park road off County Road 64.6 about 2 km by water from Early Settlers. The RV sites are gravel pull-ins on the edge of a large gravel lot, partly shaded by oak brush, with the lake on three sides. --Claude

sites.note: Two Basic sites (403, 404) with 60-ft gravel driveways, both listed for vehicles to 60 ft; site 402 is a tent-only site and is not counted.

facilities.note: The park's dump station is near Early Settlers (closes about Oct 31). CPW states nothing about toilets or water at Island; the camper services building with showers and flush toilets is in Early Settlers.

season.note: CPW: no campsites are available in the winter, and the brochure says the campgrounds are open in spring, summer and fall; no opening or closing dates are published. cpwshop's site page says 'Open year round', which CPW's own pages contradict.

booking.note: A reservation is required: cpwshop.com or 1-800-244-5613, up to six months ahead. 14 days within a 28-day period; six people, two motorized vehicles and one camping unit per site. Check-in 1 p.m., check-out noon. Display a vehicle pass.

fees.note: Both RV sites are basic: $28 a night in June 2027, Saturday the same. Plus tax, CPW's per-stay reservation fee, and a daily vehicle pass ($10-$15 per CPW's park page) or an annual state parks pass.

excluded.name: Vega State Park (Pioneer)
excluded.reason: Walk-in tent campground: CPW's camping page names '10 walk-in tent sites in the Pioneer Campground' and cpwshop types all 10 'Tent'; the five Pioneer cabins are cabins. Not a drive-in RV campground.

flags: cpwshop's GIS points for the Island sites (403 at 39.22975,-107.81497, 404 at 39.2285,-107.8134, 402 at 39.22794,-107.81261) fall 1.6 km west of the peninsula, in unbroken scrub beside the entrance road near the entrance station, with no pads or spurs on 2024 imagery: a placeholder, not the sites. The pin comes from imagery instead: the two occupied gravel bays (an RV and a pickup with a tent spot) on the west edge of the gravel lot inside OSM's 'Island Campground' polygon (way 804395680, operator CPW), median of 39.22857,-107.7964 and 39.22876,-107.79636. Which bay is 403 and which 404 is not recoverable.

CPW's camping page counts 'four campgrounds' and 109 sites (34 + 28 + 37 + 10 per the brochure), so Island is not among them there; it appears on CPW's park page ('the Island campground and day-use area'), the brochure map and boating text, and on cpwshop as loop 51550 with site ids 6319-6321, newer than the other loops' - probably a later addition. Nothing calls it overflow, host or group camping; it is sold site-by-site to the public at the basic rate.

The two RV sites are pull-ins on the edge of a large gravel lot (probably also day-use/boat-trailer parking). They are designated, numbered and reservable with tent pad, fire pit and picnic table, so not a parking-lot allowance, but the setting is lot-edge camping.

Waterfront: lakeview rests on an overhead read; the shore is 65-80 m away across grass with scattered shrub clumps, so the sightline from the pads is likely but not certain. If that is judged unconfirmed, the fallback is 'not waterfront'. Lakefront is out on distance either way.
Aggregators (campscanner) claim electric hookups and showers at Island; CPW's own pages contradict this (Early Settlers is the only campground with hookups). Ignored.
